cities.overview:
Atlanta is the biggest rental market in the Southeast and the most institutional single-family market in America. The typical home value is about $387,000 as of mid 2026, down 2.9% year over year, while 3-bed houses still rent near $2,300 and citywide rents ticked up about 1.5%. Prices soft, rents firm: that spread is why buyers who waited out 2024 and 2025 are writing offers again, and why sellers are conceding on price and repairs.

You are not the only investor who noticed. John Burns data from July 2025 put institutional ownership of Atlanta's single-family rental stock at 27.9%, the highest share in the country, roughly 72,000 houses held by large landlords. That cuts both ways: rent comps are deep and exit liquidity is real, but the cleanest 3/2s in the $250K to $320K band get cash offers fast. Metro rental vacancy runs about 9.3% on the back of a huge apartment supply wave, and that pressure lands mostly on Class A towers, not workforce houses.

Where deals pencil: at the citywide median with 20% down, the DSCR math lands around 0.8, so Atlanta is a structuring market, not a plug-and-play one. Investors make it work west and south of downtown, in Grove Park, West End, Adair Park, and the Lakewood side of the Southside, where $265K to $330K buys a renovated bungalow renting $1,950 to $2,300, and where BeltLine trail segments keep pulling both rents and values uphill.
cities.regulationNote: Georgia has no rent control and Fulton County dispossessory cases move quickly by national standards, so long-term landlords operate with few constraints; the regulated corner of this market is short-term rentals, not leases.

localAngle.title: Atlanta caps STRs at your primary residence plus one. Underwrite the lease.
localAngle.body: Atlanta's short-term rental ordinance, adopted in 2021 with enforcement live since March 2023, requires an STR license and ties it to occupancy: a host can license their primary residence plus one additional dwelling unit, and the city is explicit that nobody has two primary residences. That structure effectively blocks non-resident investors from building an STR portfolio inside city limits, and enforcement attention ramped up around the 2026 World Cup matches hosted in Atlanta. The practical read for DSCR buyers: treat any Atlanta single-family purchase as a long-term rental first. DSCR lenders here qualify files on the appraiser's market rent schedule, and your matched specialist can structure the loan so it pencils on the lease, leaving any licensed STR income as upside rather than the thing holding the approval together.

faqItems.question: How do Atlanta property taxes hit an investor's DSCR math?
faqItems.answer: Harder than most people expect. An investor purchase in the city of Atlanta carries the combined Fulton County, city, and Atlanta Public Schools levies with no homestead exemption, roughly 1.5% of value per year in effective terms. On a $265,000 house that is about $340 a month before principal, interest, or insurance. Fulton also reassesses, so underwrite at your purchase price, not the seller's old assessed value, and protest the assessment annually. Your matched specialist will run the ratio on the real post-sale tax number before you go under contract.

faqItems.question: Can I run an Airbnb in Atlanta with a DSCR loan?
faqItems.answer: Only in a narrow lane. Atlanta's ordinance ties STR licenses to a host's primary residence plus one additional unit, so a pure investor cannot stack licensed short-term rentals inside the city, and enforcement has been active since 2023 with extra attention around the 2026 World Cup. Most DSCR lenders qualify Atlanta single-family files on long-term market rent from the appraisal, not nightly-rate projections. If a deal only works as an Airbnb, that is a fragile Atlanta deal. Your matched specialist can structure the file so the property carries itself on a lease.

faqItems.question: Am I competing with Wall Street for Atlanta rentals?
faqItems.answer: In certain boxes, yes. Institutional landlords owned about 27.9% of Atlanta's single-family rental stock as of July 2025, the highest share in the country, concentrated in clean 3/2s in suburban school districts. Two practical responses: move faster with financing that behaves like cash, which is what DSCR pre-approvals through your matched specialist are built for, or buy what the algorithms skip, intown bungalows, small multifamily, and light-rehab houses in Grove Park, West End, and the Southside. The institutional presence also means deep rent comps and real exit liquidity when you sell.

faqItems.question: Prices fell 2.9% this year. Should I wait?
faqItems.answer: The correction is the reason 2026 buyers are getting terms 2021 buyers dreamed about: seller concessions, inspection repairs, and appraisals that come in clean. Rents on workforce houses barely moved, so the rent-to-price ratio that DSCR qualification lives on has quietly improved. The caveat is thin-margin BRRRR projects, where you should build cushion into your after-repair value rather than betting on a fast rebound. DSCR lenders underwrite today's value and today's rent. If those two numbers work at your entry, the direction of the next 12 months matters a lot less.

faqItems.question: Which Atlanta submarkets clear the DSCR ratio right now?
faqItems.answer: The ones west and south of downtown. Grove Park, West End, Adair Park, and the Lakewood side of the Southside pair $265,000 to $330,000 purchase prices with $1,950 to $2,300 rents, which is where files clear 1.0 with 25% down. Buckhead condos and north-side luxury rentals usually fail the ratio because prices outrun rents, and high HOA dues make it worse. BeltLine-adjacent streets carry the strongest tenant demand on the Westside, and appraisers there have current, strong rent comps, which matters because the appraisal rent schedule is the number your file lives on.

cities.overview:
Savannah runs two rental markets at once. The tourism machine fills short-term rentals in the Historic and Victorian districts, where a 3-bed near the squares can gross more in a strong month than a suburban house grosses in a quarter. The long-term market houses the port economy: Georgia Ports Authority traffic, Gulfstream Aerospace, and the Hyundai Metaplant workforce west of town. The typical home value is about $327,000 as of mid 2026, down 2.9% year over year, with 3-bed houses renting around $2,100 and flat year over year.

Two honest warnings. First, apartment vacancy runs around 11% because a supply wave hit the metro in 2024 and 2025; that pain concentrates in new Class A complexes, while historic-district housing and single-family rentals lease on a different clock. Second, carrying costs are the highest of any Georgia market on this site: Savannah city property carries roughly 40.5 combined mills, about 1.62% effective for an investor, and coastal wind exposure pushes landlord insurance meaningfully above interior Georgia. Both numbers go in the underwriting or the underwriting is fiction.

At the citywide median with 20% down the DSCR math lands near 0.82, so long-term Savannah files need submarket selection or structure. What actually clears: Eastside workforce houses bought under $200K, Southside brick ranches with steady tenants, and legally permitted STRs underwritten on projected short-term income where the zoning allows them.

localAngle.title: Savannah's STR map is mostly full. The permit decides the deal.
localAngle.body: Savannah caps non-owner-occupied short-term vacation rentals at 20% of residential parcels per ward in the Downtown and Victorian districts, and as of early 2026 eight of the ten capped wards are full, with waitlists that can run two years or more. Permits do not transfer on sale, owner-occupied units are exempt from the cap, and 2025 updates added a $1,000,000 liability insurance minimum and a 45-minute response requirement for rental agents. Chatham County added a moratorium on new unincorporated-county licenses in July 2026. Where investors still get in: the Streetcar District's TN-2 zoning west of the Historic District permits non-owner-occupied STVRs without the ward cap, and that is where STR-DSCR files belong. DSCR lenders will underwrite projected short-term income there, and your matched specialist can structure the file on nightly income or fall back to the lease if the parcel's status is anything less than certain.

faqItems.question: Can I still buy a Savannah Airbnb with a DSCR loan in 2026?
faqItems.answer: Yes, but the parcel picks you. Eight of the ten capped wards in the Downtown and Victorian districts are full for non-owner-occupied permits, waitlists run years, and permits die at closing rather than transferring. The clean lane is the Streetcar District, where TN-2 zoning permits investor STVRs without the ward cap. DSCR lenders that offer STR programs will qualify those files on projected nightly income. Buy a capped-ward house hoping for a permit and you own an expensive long-term rental. Your matched specialist will structure the file so it survives either outcome.

faqItems.question: How bad is coastal insurance for the DSCR ratio here?
faqItems.answer: It is the line item that kills more Savannah files than price. Wind exposure puts landlord premiums meaningfully above interior Georgia, figure roughly $290 a month at the citywide median and more for historic wood-frame construction, and the city now requires $1,000,000 in liability coverage on short-term rentals. Because DSCR divides rent by the full PITIA payment, every $100 of monthly premium moves the ratio by a few hundredths of a point on a typical file. Get a bindable wind-inclusive quote before you write the offer. Your matched specialist will run the ratio on the real premium, not a mainland guess.

faqItems.question: Savannah apartment vacancy is around 11%. Does that sink a rental house?
faqItems.answer: Mostly no, and it helps buyers. The vacancy spike came from a wave of new Class A apartment complexes delivered in 2024 and 2025, which compete with each other on concessions out by the highways. Single-family houses on the Eastside and Southside, and anything walkable to the squares, rent to a different tenant who is not cross-shopping a lease-up tower. Rents for 3-bed houses held flat year over year through the supply wave, which tells you the segment's demand is intact. Underwrite honestly with a vacancy allowance, but do not price a bungalow like a B-minus apartment.

faqItems.question: What does the port economy mean for long-term rentals?
faqItems.answer: It is the quiet half of the Savannah story. Georgia Ports Authority container traffic, Gulfstream Aerospace, the hospitals, and the Hyundai Metaplant ramping west of the city fill long-term rentals with W-2 tenants who never appear in the tourism statistics. That demand lands on the Eastside, the Southside, and out toward Pooler and Port Wentworth, exactly the sub-$300K stock where DSCR math clears 1.0 without nightly income. A portfolio built on port-economy leases with one legally permitted STR on top is the structure local investors keep converging on, and it is a file your matched specialist can present cleanly to 70+ lenders.

faqItems.question: How do Savannah property taxes compare for an investor?
faqItems.answer: They are the heaviest in Georgia on this site. A city of Savannah investor property stacks county, school, city, and transit levies to roughly 40.5 mills, about 1.62% of market value per year at Georgia's 40% assessment ratio with no homestead exemption. On a $327,000 house that is around $440 a month inside your PITIA before insurance. The number is fully knowable before you offer, so there is no excuse for finding it at closing. Your matched specialist will underwrite the full post-sale tax load up front, because a Savannah file that only pencils on the seller's old bill does not pencil.

cities.overview:
Augusta is what a cash-flow market looks like in 2026. The typical home value is about $189,000, up 1.9% year over year, while 3-bed houses rent around $1,450 to $1,650 depending on the pocket. Run the standard formula at 20% down and the citywide median produces a DSCR around 1.09, above 1.0 at the median, which Atlanta, Savannah, and Athens cannot claim. Property taxes help: Augusta-Richmond County's urban district levies about 28.9 mills, roughly 1.16% effective for an investor, modest by Georgia standards.

The demand story is federal. Fort Eisenhower, home of US Army Cyber Command and the Cyber Center of Excellence, anchors an estimated $7.5 billion in annual regional economic impact with over $1.6 billion in infrastructure investment planned through 2028. Cyber soldiers, contractors, and clearance-holding civilians rent houses in West Augusta, Martinez, and Evans, and they pay on time. Add the Medical District, the Savannah River Site workforce, and Augusta University, and you have a tenant base far stickier than the city's size suggests.

And yes, the Masters. For one week each April, houses near Washington Road rent for five figures and owners clear tax-free income under the 14-day rule. It is a genuine bonus and a terrible underwriting basis: DSCR files here qualify on long-term market rent, and any tournament-week windfall stays what it is, a windfall. The investors who win Augusta buy the boring lease and treat April as gravy.
cities.regulationNote: Georgia's landlord-friendly framework applies fully in Augusta-Richmond County, evictions move through magistrate court quickly, there is no rent control, and short-term rentals face no citywide cap, so the operating risk here is tenant quality and property condition, not regulation.

faqItems.question: Can Masters week income help me qualify for a DSCR loan?
faqItems.answer: No, and you should not want it to. DSCR lenders qualify Augusta files on long-term market rent from the appraisal rent schedule, and a one-week income spike, however spectacular, is not a rent schedule. What Masters week actually offers is a legal bonus: rent your property for 14 or fewer days per year and federal law makes that income tax-free. Some owners clear five figures near Washington Road in a single week. Underwrite the boring 12-month lease, let the loan stand on that, and treat April as found money. Your matched specialist structures the file exactly that way.

faqItems.question: What does Fort Eisenhower's growth actually do for landlords?
faqItems.answer: It manufactures tenants. The cyber mission at Fort Eisenhower, Army Cyber Command, the Cyber Center of Excellence, and NSA Georgia, supports an estimated $7.5 billion in annual regional impact with $1.6 billion in infrastructure investment planned through 2028. Soldiers arrive with housing allowances, contractors arrive with clearances and salaries, and both need rentals in West Augusta, Martinez, and Evans, often on two-to-three-year assignments. That is longer average tenancy and lower collection risk than typical for a market this cheap. The play is buying the ordinary 3/2 in the commuter corridors those tenants already use.

faqItems.question: Augusta houses are cheap. Is there a minimum DSCR loan size I should know about?
faqItems.answer: Yes, and in this market it is the real constraint. Many DSCR lenders set minimum loan amounts around $75,000 to $100,000, so a $90,000 South Augusta house at 80% financing produces a $72,000 loan that plenty of lenders will not write. Your options: buy slightly better stock so the loan clears the floor, put less down to keep the loan size up, or bundle several cheap houses into one portfolio DSCR loan. faqItems.question: Where does the DSCR math work best in Augusta right now?

A renovated 3/2 in South Augusta at $175,000 renting $1,395 clears a 1.15 ratio with 25% down at today's costs, which is why BRRRR investors keep recycling capital there. West Augusta costs more and the ratio lands closer to 1.0, but cyber-workforce tenants stay longer and the houses need less. Summerville is the appreciation and Masters-demand play, not the cash-flow play. Most Augusta portfolios end up holding a mix, and lenders have no problem with that.

Columbus is a military rental market with a river town attached. The typical home value is about $177,000 as of mid 2026, up 2.3% year over year, and homes go pending in around 16 days, the fastest of any Georgia market on this site. Citywide rents softened about 3.5% over the past year as new supply leased up, but 3-bed houses still pull around $1,350, and the citywide DSCR math at 20% down lands right at 1.03, above water at the median.

The demand anchor is Fort Benning, which got its name back in March 2025 after two years as Fort Moore, now honoring World War I hero Cpl. Fred Benning. As the Army's Maneuver Center of Excellence it cycles tens of thousands of soldiers, instructors, and families through the area, and the ones who live off-post arrive with a housing allowance and a report date. That produces fast leasing near the gates and along the Macon Road and Buena Vista Road corridors, with the tradeoff every military landlord knows: PCS season turnover, roughly every two to three years.

Beyond the base, TSYS and the Synovus banking cluster employ downtown, Piedmont and St. Francis run the hospitals, and the whitewater course keeps pulling Atlanta weekenders to a riverfront that looked very different fifteen years ago. Investors here win by buying renovated 3/2s in East Columbus and Midtown in the $150K to $200K band, renting to BAH-backed tenants, and underwriting the turnover honestly instead of pretending it away.

For landlords that means reliable rent and fast leasing near the gates, paired with predictable turnover as tenants PCS every two to three years. DSCR lenders treat military-heavy markets like any other on paper, the file qualifies on the appraisal's market rent, but smart underwriting adds a vacancy and re-lease allowance for PCS season. Your matched specialist can structure the ratio with enough cushion that a summer turnover does not turn a 1.05 file into a personal cash call.

faqItems.answer: Good for the loan, demanding on operations. DSCR qualification runs on the property's market rent, and appraisers in Columbus have deep comps because the rental pool is huge. Operationally, BAH-backed tenants pay reliably and lease quickly, but they leave on orders roughly every two to three years, so your real-world numbers need a re-lease allowance every couple of summers. Your matched specialist can structure the down payment so the file clears with margin, which is what turns PCS season from a crisis into a calendar event.

faqItems.question: Does the Fort Moore / Fort Benning renaming change anything for investors?
faqItems.answer: Nothing economic. The post was renamed Fort Moore in 2023 and restored to Fort Benning in March 2025 honoring a different Benning, Cpl. Fred Benning of World War I. The mission that matters to landlords, the Maneuver Center of Excellence and its constant rotation of trainees, instructors, and support staff, never moved. If anything, the episode is a reminder to underwrite the mission rather than the headlines: as long as infantry and armor training lives here, off-post rental demand in East Columbus and along the gate corridors is structural, not cyclical.

Meanwhile prices rose 2.3% and homes go pending in about 16 days, which is not what a weakening market looks like. For a DSCR buyer the honest read is: underwrite today's rent, not 2022's, and favor single-family over anything competing directly with a lease-up special. At a $177,000 median with rents at these levels, the ratio math still clears 1.0 citywide, softness and all.

Rents are proportionate, a 3-bed house pulls roughly $1,200 to $1,350, and the citywide DSCR math at 20% down lands at about 0.99, a rounding error from 1.0 before you even pick a submarket. Taxes are the quiet advantage: Macon-Bibb has cut its millage five consecutive years, and the combined county-plus-school levy of about 24.25 mills works out near 0.97% effective for an investor, the lowest of any Georgia market on this site.

The economy is steadier than the price tag implies. Atrium Health Navicent's medical center is the region's anchor employer, GEICO runs a major regional office, Mercer University adds students and staff, and the I-75 and I-16 interchange keeps warehouse and logistics payrolls growing. An hour and a half down I-75 from Atlanta, Macon also catches investors priced out of that market, which partly explains the 71-mile-radius license plates at every courthouse auction.

The catch is financing mechanics, not fundamentals. Much of Macon's stock is cheap enough that an 80% loan falls below the $75,000 to $100,000 minimum loan amounts many DSCR lenders enforce. The investors who scale here either buy the $140K-plus renovated stock, or bundle houses into portfolio loans. Structure, not luck.
cities.regulationNote: Macon-Bibb is about as landlord-friendly as American markets get, no rent control, quick magistrate-court dispossessory process, no STR caps, and a government that has cut the property tax levy five years running; your real risks are property condition and tenant screening, not rules.

localAngle.title: Sub-$200K houses everywhere. The question is the lender's minimum loan amount.
localAngle.body: Macon's superpower and its financing problem are the same fact: the houses are cheap. A $176,000 citywide median means an enormous share of investable stock prices between $80,000 and $150,000, and with 80% loans the bottom half of that range produces balances of $64,000 to $100,000. Many DSCR lenders will not write below $75,000, and plenty draw the line at $100,000 or $150,000, so the deal that pencils beautifully on rent-to-price can still die in program guidelines. Three structures solve it. Buy the $140,000-plus renovated stock in Ingleside or Vineville so the loan clears common floors. Put less down on small purchases so the loan amount stays above the minimum. Or bundle three to five cheap houses into a single portfolio DSCR loan with one payment and one closing. Your matched specialist knows which of the 70+ lenders in the network go low on loan size and which want the portfolio wrapper, which is exactly the kind of matching problem this site exists to solve.

faqItems.question: Why do DSCR lenders reject cheap Macon houses that cash flow great?
faqItems.answer: Minimum loan amounts. A $90,000 house with 80% financing needs a $72,000 loan, and many DSCR lenders set floors at $75,000 or $100,000 regardless of how well the deal pencils. It is a program guideline, not a judgment on your deal. The workarounds are mechanical: buy slightly better stock so the loan clears the floor, reduce the down payment so the loan amount rises, or bundle several houses into one portfolio loan. Your matched specialist knows which of the 70+ lenders write small-balance files and which need the bundle, and matching that correctly is the whole game in Macon.

faqItems.question: Is Macon's low property tax real, and will it last?
faqItems.answer: It is real today: Macon-Bibb has reduced its millage five consecutive years, landing at 9.575 mills for 2025, and with the Bibb school levy at 14.674 the combined load is about 24.25 mills, roughly 0.97% of market value for an investor at Georgia's 40% assessment ratio. That is the lightest tax drag of any Georgia market on this site and it is worth a meaningful chunk of DSCR ratio on every file. No one can promise future budgets, so underwrite the current number and enjoy it, but do not build a thesis that requires taxes to keep falling.

faqItems.question: Who actually rents houses in Macon?
faqItems.answer: Hospital staff, insurance and logistics payrolls, and Mercer-affiliated tenants. Atrium Health Navicent anchors the medical corridor that Ingleside and Vineville feed, GEICO's regional office employs thousands, and the I-75/I-16 interchange keeps adding warehouse jobs. That mix rents $1,100 to $1,400 houses all day and is far less cyclical than a single-employer town. Screening matters more here than in pricier metros because the tenant pool is wide: the difference between a 1.15 file performing and disappointing is usually collections discipline, not the market. Buy the corridor, screen hard, and Macon behaves.

faqItems.question: Should I expect appreciation in Macon or just cash flow?
faqItems.answer: Underwrite for cash flow and let appreciation surprise you. Values rose 2.3% over the past year, which is healthy but modest, and Macon has never been a boom market. What it offers instead is entry math that works at the median, near-1.0 DSCR citywide at 20% down before submarket selection, and a tax structure that keeps operating costs low while you hold. Investors chasing equity growth put their money 85 miles north and accept negative carry to get it. Investors who want the payment covered from month one keep choosing Macon. Know which trade you are making.

cities.hook: Athens homes average $344K on the back of 43,888 UGA students, and 3-bed houses rent near $1,900. Occupancy is bulletproof, entry is expensive, and the DSCR math takes real structuring.
cities.metaDescription: Athens homes average $344K with UGA driving 3-bed rents near $1,900. See how DSCR lenders treat student rentals. Match with a DSCR loan specialist.
cities.overview:
Athens is a university town with university-town math. The University of Georgia enrolled a record 43,888 students in fall 2025, and that engine keeps the typical home value at about $344,000, up 1.9% year over year, while 3-bed houses rent near $1,900 and vacancy runs tight. Rents rose about 1.7% over the past year. Demand is not the problem here; price is. At the citywide median with 20% down, the DSCR formula produces roughly 0.77, the weakest headline ratio of any Georgia market on this site, which is exactly why Athens files get structured instead of rubber-stamped.

The student-rental economy is its own discipline. Close to campus, houses lease by the bed at $600 to $800 per room on 12-month leases signed the previous fall, so a 4-bed near Milledge Avenue can gross $2,600 to $3,000 while the same house six miles out rents whole for $1,800. Competition is real: purpose-built student housing towers keep delivering downtown, and UGA opens a 566-bed first-year residence hall in fall 2026. New towers compete on amenities; older houses compete on price and porch. Both keep filling.

Beyond campus, Piedmont Athens Regional and St. Mary's anchor healthcare employment, Boehringer Ingelheim and the poultry-science complex add industry, and Atlanta commuters push demand on the west side. The non-student play, Eastside 3/2s renting to families and hospital staff, is quieter, cheaper, and often the cleaner DSCR file.
cities.regulationNote: Georgia's landlord-friendly baseline applies, but Athens-Clarke zoning restricts how many unrelated tenants can share a house in single-family districts, which caps the by-the-bed model outside multifamily zones, so verify the parcel's zoning before underwriting a per-room pro forma.

neighborhoods.name: Five Points
neighborhoods.note: The blue-chip student address south of campus. Per-bed leasing at premium rents, pre-leased a year ahead, but entry prices mean the ratio needs interest-only or a heavy down payment.

neighborhoods.name: Baxter / Milledge corridor
neighborhoods.note: Walk-to-campus 4-beds that lease by the room every fall. The strongest gross rents per dollar of any student pocket, and the natural home for structured DSCR files.

neighborhoods.name: Normaltown / Boulevard
neighborhoods.note: Historic bungalows near the medical campus renting to residents, professors, and grad students. Lower turnover than undergrad blocks, better appreciation than the Eastside.

neighborhoods.name: Eastside (Gaines School / Cedar Creek)
neighborhoods.note: The non-student play: 1970s-90s 3/2s renting to families and hospital staff. Cheapest entry in the county and the cleanest whole-house DSCR math in Athens.

localAngle.title: 43,888 Bulldogs need housing. DSCR lenders fund it, on their terms.
localAngle.body: UGA's fall 2025 enrollment hit a record 43,888, and the university's own beds cover only a fraction of it, so private landlords house the rest on a rhythm every Athens investor learns fast: 12-month leases signed the previous fall, by-the-bed pricing near campus, and one brutal truth, miss the August cycle and the house can sit until January. DSCR lenders finance student rentals, but on their terms. The file qualifies on the appraiser's whole-house market rent, not your per-room pro forma, some lenders cap bedroom counts or sour on leases with four separate signers, and Athens-Clarke zoning limits unrelated occupants in single-family districts, which can quietly invalidate a per-bed plan. Competition is also arriving: purpose-built student towers keep delivering downtown and UGA opens a 566-bed residence hall in fall 2026, pressure that lands hardest on mediocre product at premium prices. Your matched specialist knows which of the 70+ lenders are comfortable with student files and structures the ratio on numbers an appraiser will actually support.

faqItems.question: Do DSCR lenders actually finance student rentals in Athens?
faqItems.answer: Yes, with three caveats that decide the outcome. First, qualification runs on the appraiser's whole-house market rent, so a per-bed pro forma that grosses $3,000 does not help if the 1007 form says $2,600. Second, some lenders cap bedroom counts, dislike four-signer leases, or decline student-heavy files outright, so lender selection matters more here than in most markets. Third, Athens-Clarke zoning limits unrelated occupants in single-family districts, which can make a per-room plan illegal on the wrong parcel. Your matched specialist screens for all three before you spend appraisal money.

faqItems.question: What is the August lease-cycle risk everyone mentions?
faqItems.answer: Athens student rentals lease on one calendar. Students sign 12-month leases in the preceding fall and move in August; a house that misses that window can sit half-empty until the spring semester, sometimes longer. That risk does not appear in the DSCR calculation, which uses market rent, but it absolutely appears in your bank account. Practical defenses: buy pre-leased when possible, list renewal season aggressively early, and hold reserves for one missed cycle. If the payment only works with twelve perfect months, the structure is too tight, and your matched specialist can build in more cushion.

faqItems.question: Will the new student housing towers crush older rental houses?
faqItems.answer: They compete, but not head-on. Purpose-built student housing keeps delivering downtown and UGA adds a 566-bed first-year hall in fall 2026, which pressures rents on dated mid-tier apartments most directly. Houses in Five Points and along Milledge sell something a tower cannot: a porch, a yard, five friends under one roof, and proximity to game day. That product has stayed pre-leased through every construction cycle. The vulnerable asset is the mediocre house at a premium price. Buy either the irreplaceable location or the Eastside value play, and the towers become background noise.

faqItems.question: Is there a non-student way to invest in Athens?
faqItems.answer: The Eastside, and it is often the better DSCR file. Gaines School and Cedar Creek 3/2s run around $285,000 and rent near $1,750 to families, hospital staff from Piedmont Athens Regional, and university employees who want nothing to do with undergrad blocks. Turnover is lower, August means nothing, and the whole-house lease is exactly what a DSCR appraisal wants to see. The ratio still needs a healthy down payment at Athens prices, but the file is simpler and the operations are quieter. Plenty of Athens portfolios pair one campus-adjacent student house with two Eastside workhorses.

faqItems.question: How do Athens property taxes treat an investor?
faqItems.answer: Moderately, by Georgia standards. The Athens-Clarke unified government levied 12.45 mills for 2025 and the Clarke County School District 18.8, about 31.25 combined, which works out near 1.25% of market value for an investor at the state's 40% assessment ratio, with no homestead exemption softening it. On a $380,000 student house that is roughly $396 a month inside the payment. It sits between Macon's light load and Savannah's heavy one, and it is fully predictable, so the only mistake available is underwriting the seller's exempted bill instead of your own. Your matched specialist runs the investor number from the start.

cities.metaDescription: Marietta averages $481K but Fair Oaks and south Cobb buy near $315K with rents over $2,000. See where the DSCR math works and match with a specialist.
cities.overview:
Marietta is Cobb County's employment anchor wearing a suburb's clothes. The typical home value sits near $481,000 as of mid 2026, down 1.6% year over year, while 3-bed houses rent around $2,300. That citywide math is rough, but Marietta is really three markets: the expensive east Cobb pocket that carries a Walton and Pope school premium, the mid-priced core around the Square, and the workforce south side where the numbers actually pencil.

The tenant base is unusually durable for a suburb. Lockheed Martin's 8-million-square-foot plant supports more than 5,600 local jobs and announced 1,200 more Marietta-based positions in June 2026. Dobbins Air Reserve Base sits on the same runway, WellStar Kennestone is one of the busiest hospitals in Georgia, and Life University keeps a steady stream of graduate students renting close to campus. Metro Atlanta rental vacancy runs about 8.2%, but most of that pressure is new Class A apartments, not the 3-bed houses these tenants actually want.

Where deals pencil: Fair Oaks and the Franklin Gateway corridor, where $300,000 to $330,000 buys a rentable 3/2 pulling $2,000 to $2,100. One structural note: city-limits properties pay the Marietta City Schools stack at about 31.2 mills, roughly 1.25% effective for an investor, while unincorporated Marietta addresses are taxed on the Cobb schedule. Confirm which side of the line your address sits on before you underwrite.
cities.regulationNote: Georgia bans rent control statewide and Cobb evictions move quickly, so long-term landlords face few constraints; short-term rentals are the exception, with Cobb County and Marietta both regulating STRs tightly in single-family areas.

neighborhoods.note: Unincorporated pocket between Dobbins and the Square. Sub-$330K 3/2s renting over $2,000 make this the cleanest DSCR entry in Marietta.

neighborhoods.note: The city has poured redevelopment money into this stretch. Older stock at the lowest price points in Marietta proper, with steady workforce tenant demand.

neighborhoods.name: East Cobb (Marietta addresses)
neighborhoods.note: Walton and Pope school districts push prices far past what rents support. Appreciation and school-demand play, not a cash-flow play, at 20% down.

localAngle.title: Lockheed, Dobbins, and Life University keep Marietta's 3-bed rentals full.
localAngle.body: Marietta's rental demand is anchored by institutions that do not follow the housing cycle. Lockheed Martin supports more than 5,600 jobs at its Marietta facility and announced 1,200 additional local positions in June 2026. Dobbins Air Reserve Base shares the flight line and adds reservists, contractors, and visiting crews who rent rather than buy. Life University students and WellStar Kennestone hospital staff fill in the rest. The practical read for a DSCR file: appraisal rent schedules in south and central Marietta come back strong because tenant demand is deep at the $1,900 to $2,300 level, exactly where Fair Oaks and Franklin Gateway houses rent. The school-driven east side is the opposite, prices outrun rents and ratios fail. Your matched specialist can structure around that split, keeping the file in the submarkets where the appraisal rent actually covers the payment.

faqItems.question: Why is the DSCR math so different across Marietta?
faqItems.answer: Because Marietta is three markets sharing one name. East Cobb addresses carry a school premium that pushes typical values past $565,000 while rents top out near $2,850, so ratios fail badly. The core around the Square is middle ground. The south side, Fair Oaks and Franklin Gateway, is where $300,000 to $330,000 houses rent for $2,000 or more and files clear 1.0 with a bigger down payment. DSCR lenders do not care about the school district, they care about rent over payment. Your matched specialist will run the ratio by pocket, not by the citywide average, before you write an offer.

faqItems.question: How do Marietta property taxes work for an investor?
faqItems.answer: Inside the city limits you pay the City of Marietta stack, about 31.2 mills across county, city, and Marietta City Schools, which works out to roughly 1.25% of market value for an investor with no homestead exemption. Unincorporated Cobb addresses with Marietta mailing addresses are taxed on the county schedule instead, which lands a bit lower. The trap is underwriting off the seller's exempted tax bill: Cobb reassesses and an investor gets no homestead break. Your matched specialist will build the tax line from the purchase price and the correct millage before locking the ratio.

faqItems.question: Can I run a short-term rental in Marietta with a DSCR loan?
faqItems.answer: Plan on long-term rent, not nightly income. Cobb County adopted short-term rental rules in 2022 with occupancy and parking limits, and Marietta is restrictive about STRs in single-family zoning, so the regulatory footing is narrow. Most DSCR lenders in this market qualify single-family files on the appraisal's long-term market rent anyway. If a Marietta deal only pencils on Airbnb projections, it is fragile twice over, once at the city and once at the lender. Structure it to carry itself on a lease, and treat any STR income as upside rather than the basis of qualification.

faqItems.question: Is Lockheed concentration a risk for Marietta rentals?
faqItems.answer: It is worth understanding but it cuts the other way right now. Lockheed's Marietta plant supports more than 5,600 jobs and announced 1,200 additional positions in June 2026, on top of 75 years of continuous production. Dobbins Air Reserve Base, WellStar Kennestone, and Life University diversify the base further, and none of them behave like a single private employer. For underwriting, the concentration shows up as strength: appraisers can document deep tenant demand at workforce rent levels, which keeps market rent schedules firm. A portfolio spread across south Marietta pockets is not living on one paycheck.

faqItems.question: Prices in Marietta slipped 1.6% this year. Should I wait?
faqItems.answer: The slip is what makes the math close. Values are down 1.6% year over year while 3-bed rents hold near $2,300 citywide, so the rent-to-price ratio a DSCR lender divides is improving. Sellers on the south side are negotiating on price and repairs in a way they were not in 2022. DSCR loans qualify on today's rent against today's payment, and today's spread in Fair Oaks and Franklin Gateway clears 1.0 at 30% down. Waiting for a lower price risks giving back more in rate environment and competition than the discount is worth. Buy where the ratio already works.

cities.hook: The typical City of Decatur listing tops $600K against $3,100 house rents, math that fails every DSCR floor at 20% down. Investors here either buy the school premium on a No-Ratio file or buy the other Decatur, the unincorporated side.
cities.metaDescription: City of Decatur medians top $600K and DSCR math runs weak at 20% down. See the No-Ratio play and the cheaper DeKalb side. Match with a DSCR specialist.
cities.overview:
Decatur is the most misunderstood address in metro Atlanta investing, because "Decatur" is two different markets wearing the same zip-code family. The City of Decatur proper, roughly the 30030 core, is a 4-square-mile school-premium market where the median listing runs about $620,000 and 3-bed houses rent near $3,100 to $3,200. Unincorporated DeKalb County with Decatur mailing addresses, most of 30032, 30034, and 30035, is a workforce market where the same money buys two houses. Zillow's blended value for all Decatur addresses is about $283,000, which tells you how wide the gap is.

City-proper math at 20% down does not work, and pretending otherwise is how investors get hurt here. The City Schools of Decatur premium is real, homes near Decatur High command some of the strongest demand in the metro, but the city assesses at 50% of value with a 20.30 mill school levy plus about 11.2 city mills and the DeKalb county layer on top. Call it roughly 1.95% effective for an investor. Rent does not scale with the premium.

So Decatur splits into two honest plays. Inside the city: an appreciation and tenant-quality hold financed as a No-Ratio file, where no DSCR floor applies and the negative carry is a deliberate cost of owning the school premium. Outside the city: Belvedere Park and Candler-McAfee, where $260,000 to $310,000 houses rent for $1,650 to $1,750 and standard files get close on ratio. Know which Decatur your contract is in before you underwrite anything.
cities.regulationNote: Georgia law preempts rent control everywhere including the City of Decatur, and DeKalb evictions follow standard state process, so the real investor cost here is the city-proper tax stack, not landlord regulation.

neighborhoods.note: City-proper bungalow district near Decatur High. The definitive school-premium hold: weak ratio, elite tenant demand, long appreciation track record. No-Ratio territory.

neighborhoods.name: Belvedere Park
neighborhoods.note: Unincorporated DeKalb with a Decatur mailing address. Half the price basis of the city, DeKalb-schedule taxes, and brick ranches that rent all day at $1,700 plus.

neighborhoods.name: Candler-McAfee
neighborhoods.note: The cheapest Decatur-address entry. Rent-to-price is the best in the area, condition varies widely, so budget the inspection and rehab line honestly.

localAngle.title: The Decatur address trap: city limits or mailing address changes your whole file.
localAngle.body: Every street in this area says Decatur on the envelope, but only the 4-square-mile City of Decatur pays City of Decatur taxes and prices in the City Schools of Decatur premium. The city assesses property at 50% of value for its own levies, DeKalb uses 40%, and the combined city, school, and county stack lands near 1.95% effective for an investor, among the heaviest in the metro. Cross the city line into unincorporated DeKalb and the same mailing address drops to a DeKalb-schedule tax bill and a price basis that is often $300,000 lighter. That single boundary decides your tax line, your purchase price, and whether the file qualifies on ratio at all. Before you underwrite, pull the parcel in DeKalb's GIS and confirm jurisdiction, do not trust the listing. Your matched specialist will build the tax line from the actual taxing authority, then pick the program to match: standard DSCR outside the line, No-Ratio inside it.

faqItems.question: How do I know if a property is in the City of Decatur or just has a Decatur address?
faqItems.answer: Pull the parcel in DeKalb County's GIS or check the tax bill for a City of Decatur line item, and do it before you write the offer. The city is only about 4 square miles, while Decatur mailing addresses sprawl across a much larger slice of unincorporated DeKalb. The difference is not cosmetic: city parcels are assessed at 50% of value for city and school levies with a combined investor load near 1.95%, and they price in the City Schools of Decatur premium. Unincorporated parcels tax on DeKalb's 40% schedule at a lower total. Same envelope, completely different underwriting.

faqItems.question: Does a DSCR loan even work when the ratio is 0.74?
faqItems.answer: Not as a standard file, and nobody honest will pretend otherwise. This is what No-Ratio DSCR exists for: the lender qualifies the deal on credit, reserves, and a lower maximum LTV, commonly around 70%, without applying a coverage floor. Investors use it in city-proper Decatur because the asset case is appreciation and tenant quality, not monthly spread. You are consciously paying a carry cost to own a scarce asset near Decatur High. If the negative cash flow is a surprise rather than a plan, this is the wrong submarket; buy in Belvedere Park instead. Your matched specialist prices both paths so you can compare them.

faqItems.question: Where does the DSCR math actually work near Decatur?
faqItems.answer: On the unincorporated side. Belvedere Park runs about $310,000 with rents near $1,750, and Candler-McAfee sits near $260,000 with rents around $1,650. Those rent-to-price ratios are close to double what the city proper offers, and the DeKalb tax schedule is meaningfully lighter than the city stack. Files there get to workable coverage with 25% to 30% down, and brick ranch stock keeps insurance and maintenance predictable. The trade-off is appreciation profile and tenant screening effort. Plenty of investors run both: cash-flowing DeKalb rentals funding a No-Ratio city-proper hold.

faqItems.question: Decatur prices fell 4.6% this year. What does that mean for my file?
faqItems.answer: The blended Zillow figure for all Decatur addresses fell 4.6%, and most of that softness lives on the unincorporated side, where it improves your entry basis against rents that barely moved. City-proper values held up better, which is exactly the school-premium behavior long-term holders are buying. For a DSCR file the direction matters less than the spread: lenders divide today's appraisal rent by today's payment. A softer purchase price on a Belvedere Park ranch moves the ratio more than any market forecast. Appraisals have also been landing without drama because comps are plentiful in both submarkets.

faqItems.question: What should out-of-state investors know about DeKalb taxes and reassessment?
faqItems.answer: Two things. First, DeKalb reassesses and an investor gets no homestead exemption, so the seller's tax bill is fiction for your underwriting; build the line from your purchase price and the correct jurisdiction schedule. Second, the city-versus-unincorporated boundary can shift your effective load from roughly the mid-1s to nearly 2% of value, which on a $600,000 asset is hundreds of dollars a month of PITIA. That is often the entire difference between a passing and failing ratio. Your matched specialist runs the post-sale tax number for the actual taxing authority before the file goes to a lender, not after.

PCS season concentrates move-ins and move-outs into late spring and summer, so vacancies in Warner Robins are short but clustered, and the federal military clause lets orders-holding tenants end leases early. The honest underwrite budgets one turnover month every couple of years rather than pretending turnover never happens, and prices the rent inside the relevant BAH band rather than $100 above it. faqItems.question: What happens to my Warner Robins rental when a military tenant gets PCS orders?
faqItems.answer: Federal law, the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, lets a tenant with permanent change of station or deployment orders terminate the lease with proper notice, typically effective 30 days after the next rent due date. You cannot contract around it, so underwrite with it. In practice PCS turnover is orderly: tenants give notice, the base's housing office ecosystem refers incoming families, and summer arrival season refills vacancies quickly. Budget a turnover month every couple of years, keep the property listed with managers who work the incoming-PCS pipeline, and the military clause becomes a manageable cost instead of a surprise.

That gives you three things most markets never offer: a visible ceiling for your segment, a tenant pool whose housing budget arrives with the paycheck, and appraisers who anchor market rent schedules to the same public tables your lender will see. The discipline is pricing inside the band your target rank actually receives. A $1,600 rent under the E-5 band leases fast and collects reliably; a $1,950 rent chasing the E-6 band overshoots most of the pool.

The base employs about 21,500 people, generated $4.48 billion in reported economic impact in 2025, and its workforce is mostly career civilian employees in depot maintenance and logistics roles that have grown, not shrunk, through recent budget cycles. Base realignment decisions move slowly and publicly, nothing like a private employer's sudden exit. If you want a hedge inside the metro, the 31088 corridor leans more civilian and Bonaire leans more family-buyer, so a small portfolio here can spread across tenant types while keeping the same management footprint.

faqItems.answer: Among the lightest carrying costs in the state. The 2025 stack combines the City of Valdosta at 6.254 mills, Valdosta City Schools at 13.304, and the Lowndes County layer, landing near 1.19% of market value for an investor with no homestead exemption, about $183 a month on a $185,000 house. Insurance for inland South Georgia frame and brick stock runs moderate, typically near $120 to $150 monthly at these price points, with no coastal wind surcharge this far from the Gulf. Underwrite from your purchase price rather than the seller's exempted bill, because Lowndes reassesses on sale.

faqItems.question: Valdosta prices are up 3.5% while Atlanta falls. What is driving it, and does it hold?
faqItems.answer: The drivers are structural rather than speculative: Moody's steady personnel base, VSU's $385 million-plus economic footprint, hospital and logistics hiring, and a price level low enough that local wages still buy houses. Investor demand from out-of-market buyers chasing ratios adds a second bid under the $250,000 line. Nothing about a 3.5% gain on a $215,000 base looks frothy, and rents moved up alongside prices, so the ratio held. For underwriting purposes it barely matters: the file qualifies on today's appraisal rent against today's payment, and Bemiss-corridor deals clear 1.1 at 25% down right now.
